items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: And the piano player, Octave, got high and got homesick

ctx.x: I'll tell you about this band from New Orleans. I could only play 'My Isle of Golden Dreams,' or a few songs, or if you start a song off, you know, I could probably come in. So this band--Son Lewis and Cal Liston, who had a dance hall they called it the Skunk...well, they called it...what the hell, some dance hall in Dallas. And they used to like go to other towns and have dances two or three days a week.

So then they said...they needed a piano player. And the piano player, Octave, got high and got homesick for some of that gum-bo and, you know, just...You know, and those fellows couldn't contain themselves. They just went like insane, you know, not to do anything harmful, but just longing for home, you know? So this guy went home. And they said, "Well, we've got to have a piano player to play the dance," so they picked me. And I said to them, "Now look, I'm no piano player when it come down to this business. But…

That was agreeable, Dan. And then when we got to Mineral Wells, or Wichita Falls or wherever the hell it was, everything changed. They'd bring the music; "Now, in the fourteenth bar you will do this and do that." Now we discover that the piano is not in tune. So in order for them to play in B-flat, I would have to play in B-natural. Well, I couldn't play in B-flat too well to begin with. Now, if they're puttin' me in B-natural, I'm really in trouble. So, this night these guys start a song. I couldn't come in…
